summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with HIV, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, atrial fibrillation, and post-herpetic neuralgia was admitted after missing two dialysis sessions due to foot pain from a mechanical fall. She presented with weakness, hypotension, hyperkalemia, and elevated creatinine. Imaging showed no fractures in her toe or hip. She was treated with three hemodialysis sessions, which improved her labs and symptoms. Empiric IV vancomycin was given but discontinued after blood cultures remained negative. Her pain was managed with a fentanyl patch and a surgical shoe. She was discharged home with improved strength, stable vital signs, and plans for home health, safety evaluation, and follow-up with her HIV and nephrology teams.
problems: Knee, leg, ankle, and foot injury
